transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-02-09 16:00 UTC | Duration 47m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jared Lowe (Redwood SE), Priya Raman (Novus Medica), Aaron Wexler (CTO), Sofia Diaz (Security Lead), Liam O'Sullivan (Procurement)
Link to shared deck: https://redwood.app/decks/novus-q1-renewal (ref)

Summary (auto): quick renewal check, capacity uplift plan, EU/APAC private onboarding discussion, security clarifications requested.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i know we have about 45 minutes, we'll move quick — happy to run through the renewal terms and then hand it to Jared for the eu/apac deployment notes.
[00:18] Priya Raman: thanks Maya, yeah we wanted to make sure the renewal lines up with our fiscal cycle and also confirm the sovereignty requirements before we commit to the uplift.
[00:30] Aaron Wexler: hi, yes, timeline is key — we need eu private by end of q2 for gdpr reasons, apac can be phased later. also bandwidth: our usage pattern is spiky, daily peaks around 200 rps, primarily embeddings and chat gen.
[00:45] Jared Lowe: got it, that maps well to a reserved+burst model; we typically recommend a base reserved capacity sized for your 95th percentile steady throughput and then burst blocks for peaks. if you want we can show simulated throughput numbers — we have a little benchmark plan.
[01:05] Sofia Diaz: just to flag security — we require KMS integration, HSM-backed key wrap if possible, and audit log retention for 3 years. do you support BYOK? is the private offering in a customer-managed vpc?
[01:22] Maya Chen: yes we support BYOK via KMS and HSM integrations in our Private product; the private deployment sits in the customer's VPC with a customer-managed control plane option. i'll let Jared confirm the exact certs but from product side we can do RBAC, SSO/SAML, and long-term audit exports.
[01:40] Priya Raman: perfect but we need to see the SOC2 and iso attestation — and a redacted architecture of the private control plane. can that be provided short-form?
[01:55] Maya Chen: absolutely — we'll attach SOC 2 Type II and ISO certs, and a network diagram. i'll add that to the renewal packet.
[02:05] Liam O'Sullivan: procurement timing — we typically need 3 weeks to process an amendment. if you push pricing by feb 12 we can sign by end of feb, so the capacity is green on mar 1.
[02:20] Maya Chen: noted. we'll aim for feb 12 for the amendment.
[02:28] Jared Lowe: on the technical side, couple notes: for eu private deployments we need to size GPU pools per model. you mentioned larger embedding workloads; i suggest quantized 8-bit embeddings for cost, and we can reserve a dedicated pool for your high-priority routes to meet latency SLOs.
[02:48] Aaron Wexler: what are realistic p95 latencies for chat generation if we go dedicated eu pool vs hosted fallback? our user SLAs are 300ms for short prompts.
[03:05] Jared Lowe: depends on sequence length; for 256 tokens with a dedicated A100 pool we generally hit 120–180ms p95. hosted can be variable; we will definitely aim to pin dedicated to get below 300ms. fallback will add 100–250ms depending on region.
[03:25] Priya Raman: is the kv cache shared across nodes or per-instance? we rely on prefix caching to avoid repeated context costs.
[03:38] Jared Lowe: KV cache is local to the instance but we have a distributed cache for hot prefixes; for Private we can configure prefix cache TTLs, and we can also do application-side sharding if you want cross-node hot keys.
[03:52] Sofia Diaz: any notes on encryption at rest for KV cache? need to ensure keys are customer controlled.
[04:02] Jared Lowe: yes encryption at rest is EKM-backed in Private deployments if you use BYOK; KV shards are encrypted with those keys. there may be small differences in how we manage ephemeral keys for compute but we'll document it.
[04:18] Maya Chen: quick question for procurement — is Novus able to take a twelve-month renewal with a mid-term capacity amendment or do you need fixed-term price lock?
[04:32] Liam O'Sullivan: we'd prefer fixed pricing for 12 months but also need flexibility to add burst capacity; can we have a tiered amendment where reserved is fixed and bursts are variable?
[04:44] Maya Chen: yes that's standard — we do reserved commit + burst credits on top. i'll include a few tiered pricing rows in the amendment.
[04:55] Aaron Wexler: regarding private control plane — what's the timeline for eu region provisioning? from order to live how long?
[05:08] Jared Lowe: for EU private VPC: order -> 2–3 weeks for networking and control plane, then 1 week for model onboarding and validation — so roughly 3–4 weeks end-to-end if there's no custom compliance gating. we can accelerate if you sign earlier and give us the network team contacts.
[05:28] Priya Raman: we'd like a short perf poc in eu with 2 models and our sample workload before we commit to full reserved capacity. can you run that?
[05:40] Jared Lowe: yes — we can run a 72-hr POC at scale with the patterns you described. we'd need a test token set and a representative prompt mix.
[05:50] Priya Raman: ok i'll assemble that and share.
[05:55] Maya Chen: i'll follow up with a one-pager of the amendment and the SOW plus the compliance artifacts.
[06:02] Sofia Diaz: also, please include details about log export format and retention endpoints for SIEM integration (we use Splunk).
[06:12] Jared Lowe: we'll include a sample audit log schema and an event map for Splunk ingestion; we also have a connector we can share.
[06:22] Aaron Wexler: on the competitor note, GigaML quoted a lower unit price but didn't offer private deployment or the same SLAs. curious if we can get a price close to them with the dedicated path.
[06:36] Maya Chen: we'll try to be competitive; i'll include a pricing comparator that shows where the cost comes from (reserved vs burst vs SLO priority lanes).
[06:48] Liam O'Sullivan: procurement note — need copy of terms, indemnities, and insurance limits for legal review.
[06:57] Maya Chen: will attach.
[07:02] [crosstalk] Priya Raman: sorry one more — do you support per-route rollout (canary) within private?
[07:10] Jared Lowe: yes, we support canaries and A/B with traffic weighting and automatic fallback to an older model if error rate spikes.
[07:20] Priya Raman: good. that helps our migration plan.
[07:26] Maya Chen: quick recap — action owners, we'll aim to have amendment to you by feb 12, se runs eu perf poc and sends results by the 18th, and customer to provide compliance and procurement windows.
[07:40] Aaron Wexler: sounds good.
[07:44] Maya Chen: any final questions?
[07:47] Sofia Diaz: none from security; we'll follow up if we see gaps after we review the docs.
[07:52] Priya Raman: that's all. thanks.
[07:55] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with links and the draft amendment. bye.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hear on product names ("Red wood" instead of "Redwood"), punctuation is sparse, proper nouns may be slightly off.

End of transcript.
